name: Pho
description: Vietnam's iconic noodle soup with fragrant beef broth, rice noodles, and fresh herbs. A must-try breakfast classic in Hanoi.
cookingMethod: Bones and spices are simmered for hours to create a clear, aromatic broth. Rice noodles are blanched, topped with sliced beef, and finished with herbs and lime.

name: Bun Cha
description: Grilled pork patties and slices served with vermicelli, fresh herbs, and a sweet-savory dipping sauce.
cookingMethod: Pork is marinated and charcoal-grilled, then served in a warm dipping broth with vermicelli and herbs on the side.

name: Egg Coffee
description: A Hanoi specialty: strong coffee topped with a creamy whipped egg yolk foam that tastes like liquid tiramisu.
cookingMethod: Egg yolk is whipped with condensed milk until frothy, then poured over hot or iced Vietnamese coffee.

name: Bun Bo Hue
description: A spicy beef noodle soup from Hue with lemongrass, annatto oil, and a bold, aromatic broth.
cookingMethod: Beef and pork bones are simmered with lemongrass and spices. The broth is finished with annatto oil and chili before serving with thick round noodles.

name: Cao Lau
description: Hoi An's signature noodle dish with thick noodles, sliced pork, greens, and crispy croutons.
cookingMethod: Thick local noodles are topped with marinated pork, fresh greens, herbs, and crispy rice croutons, then lightly dressed with savory sauce.

name: Com Hen
description: A humble Hue specialty of baby clams over rice with peanuts, herbs, pork crackling, and spicy broth.
cookingMethod: Baby clams are cooked and tossed with aromatics, then served over rice with crunchy toppings and a side of spicy clam broth.

name: Banh Mi
description: A crispy baguette sandwich filled with pâté, meats, pickled vegetables, cilantro, and chili — Vietnam's beloved street sandwich.
cookingMethod: A warm crispy baguette is spread with pâté and mayo, then filled with meats, pickles, cucumber, cilantro, and chili.

name: Hu Tieu
description: A Southern noodle soup with clear pork broth, rice noodles, shrimp, and pork — light yet deeply savory.
cookingMethod: A clear pork broth is simmered and served with noodles, shrimp, sliced pork, and fresh toppings.

name: Goi Cuon
description: Fresh spring rolls wrapped in rice paper with shrimp, pork, vermicelli, and herbs, dipped in peanut or fish sauce.
cookingMethod: Softened rice paper is filled with vermicelli, herbs, shrimp, and pork, then rolled tightly and served with dipping sauce.

name: Goat Meat
description: Ninh Binh specialty goat dishes — often grilled or hotpot-style — paired with local herbs and dipping sauces.
cookingMethod: Goat is marinated with aromatics and grilled or simmered in hotpot, served with fresh herbs and dipping sauces.

name: Seafood Hotpot
description: Fresh Ha Long Bay seafood cooked in a fragrant hotpot broth with vegetables and noodles.
cookingMethod: A savory broth is brought to a boil at the table while diners cook assorted fresh seafood and vegetables.

name: Mi Quang
description: A Central Vietnamese turmeric noodle dish with a small amount of rich broth, topped with meat, peanuts, and herbs.
cookingMethod: Wide turmeric noodles are served with a shallow savory broth, protein toppings, crushed peanuts, and crispy rice crackers.
